title: Leadership townline simulated Q&A and messaging lab
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical playbook for the upcoming company townline (All-Hands). It bundles an adjusted OKR draft for exec review, a crisp exec-update script, a run-of-show for an efficient 75-minute townline, and a simulated Q&A lab to rehearse high-risk questions.

Context and constraints:
- Goal: align company on top-3 company priorities for the next 90 days and reduce follow-up clarifying questions by 60% through clearer messaging.
- Audience: ~150 employees across ENG, Product, GTM, SRE, and Customer Success. Senior leadership (CEO, CTO, CPO) will present.
- Timebox: 75 minutes live + 20 minutes optional breakout rooms.
- Non-negotiables: SLAs for dedicated customers, Private deployment roadmap clarity, and an honest update on cost-per-inference initiatives.

One-paragraph opener for CEO (30–45s):
"Hi team — quick state: we shipped Dedicated GA, doubled run-rate in two regions, and hit a significant perf milestone (p50 latency down 18% for our hosted API). But we also saw two customer incidents that exposed friction in rollout tooling. Today we’ll cover what we’re prioritizing next quarter to keep growth predictable, reduce customer risk, and lower inference costs — and we’ll leave plenty of time for questions. Short, actionable, and to-the-point."

Proposed company-level OKRs (draft):
- Objective A: Make inference predictable and cost-effective for production teams.
  - KR1: Reduce average inference cost-per-1000-tokens by 20% across hosted workloads (baseline: July 2024 internal report).
  - KR2: Achieve 99.9% availability for top-10 paying tenants on Dedicated with SLO monitoring in place.
  - KR3: Ship prefix/KV caching autopilot feature and onboard 3 customers in beta.

- Objective B: Expand private deployment adoption in regulated industries.
  - KR1: Close 5 Private pilot contracts (one in finance, two in healthcare) with signed NDAs.
  - KR2: Offer an on-prem deployment reference architecture and a hardened upgrade path (documentation + automated smoke tests).
  - KR3: Integrate with at least two major KMS/HSM providers and publish compliance artifacts.

- Objective C: Developer experience and observability that drives retention.
  - KR1: Ship token-level cost dashboards for self-serve customers; 50% of new teams use dashboards within 30 days.
  - KR2: Reduce mean time to triage by 40% for production errors via tracing hooks and improved alert templates.
  - KR3: Publish 10 eval-prompts and example prompts for common PLG use cases (search, summarization, chat).

Cascade notes (who’s owning what):
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: KR1.1, KR1.3 (cost reductions + caching autopilot). Owner: Miguel Torres.
- Product-Hosted-API: KR1.1 measurement, dashboards (C. Nguyen).
- Private-Deployments + Security: Objective B lead (Samir Patel).
- Console + Observability: Objective C owner (Evan Liu).

Exec update bullets (for 10-min slide block):
- Market & traction (2 min): top-line metrics: MRR trends, Dedicated committed capacity growth, top 5 new customers.
- Product wins (3 min): Dedicated GA, KV caching prototype completed, early perf benchmarks.
- What failed / learnings (2 min): two rollout incidents — root cause = mismatch in rollout policy vs. traffic spike; mitigation = immediate safe-fail toggles + runbook updates.
- Ask of the company (2 min): focus engineers on three ship-blockers next sprint: caching autopilot, upgrade smoke tests, and token-cost dashboards.

Run-of-show (75-minute format):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & housekeeping (People Ops): agenda, Slack channels for Qs.
- 0:05–0:13 — CEO state & top-line metrics.
- 0:13–0:23 — Product demo: Dedicated + perf wins (CPO).
- 0:23–0:33 — Engineering deep-dive: caching autopilot & rollout hardening (ENG lead).
- 0:33–0:43 — Customer success highlight + 1 customer story (CS).
- 0:43–0:55 — Roadmap & company OKRs (Product ops): show concrete owner map and milestones.
- 0:55–1:10 — Live Q&A (moderated): pre-seeded Qs + open mic.
- 1:10–1:15 — Closing, immediate asks, and how to follow up.

Slide run notes (high impact slides):
- Slide 3 (metrics): Use small multiples for latency, cost, and adoption. One-sentence insight under each chart.
- Slide 7 (incidents): A short timeline with mitigations and next steps — avoid technical jargon.
- Slide 11 (OKR matrix): Single table mapping KRs to owners, current status (R/Y/G), and next two milestones.

Rehearsal checklist (tick-box style — to be used in dry run):
- [ ] Speakers confirm one-sentence talking points (max 2 bullets each).
- [ ] Slides are in present mode and loaded on rehearsal machine.
- [ ] Backup slide deck (PDF) available to People Ops.
- [ ] Zoom/room AV test, captions enabled, recording acknowledged.
- [ ] Moderator has pre-seeded Q list and 5 backup questions.
- [ ] Incident statement draft (for potential live announcement) approved by Legal.

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk A: Customer-facing incident during townline causes PR questions. Mitigation: pre-approved incident statement + customer outreach owner.
- Risk B: Slide content leaks ahead of time. Mitigation: watermark, restrict edit permissions, embargo notice.
- Risk C: Exec-runway timing slips (overruns). Mitigation: hard cutoffs per block, moderator authority.
- Risk D: Unclear asks leading to busywork. Mitigation: define 3 specific asks and owners.
- Risk E: Technical deep-dive loses non-technical audience. Mitigation: two-tier slides: one summary + appendix.
- Risk F: High-volume live Qs unanswerable. Mitigation: triage to follow-up doc + volunteer squad to own responses.

Simulated Q&A lab (roleplay instructions for execs & moderators):
- Format: 6 min per scenario: 2 min ask, 2 min response, 2 min follow-up.
- Roles: questioner (asks), responder (exec), note-taker (captures follow-ups), moderator (time).
- Run three scenarios: customer incident, pricing/back-of-envelope cost concerns, and Private-deploy regulatory question.

Examples of high-risk Qs + model answers (practice scripts):
- Q: "Customers saw higher inference cost in August — what are you doing to prevent this recurring?"
  A: "We own the unit economics problem and have three levers: smarter batching, KV/prefix caching, and model variant routing. We shipped experiments that reduced p95 token-cost by ~12% in lab — next quarter we’ll turn on autopilot for 3 big tenants and measure real-world delta."

- Q: "Can you guarantee Private will meet SOC2/ISO timelines for enterprise customers?"
  A: "We have an explicit roadmap and two pilot customers under NDA; our integration with KMS/HSM providers is underway. We can commit to a documented upgrade and compliance checklist; sales will coordinate timelines per-customer."

- Q: "Is Dedicated sustainable for small customers?"
  A: "Dedicated is positioned for customers who need predictable latency/throughput. For smaller teams we’re improving the hosted offering and configuring burst policies to keep cost reasonable; team will publish clear runbooks in next 6 weeks."

Follow-up mechanics (post-townline):
- Within 24 hours: publish slides + recording + consolidated Q&A on Confluence.
- Within 72 hours: assign owners for each follow-up and publish triage board (Jira/Linear).
- 2-week checkpoint: status update on top-3 asks and KR baselines.

Comms templates (copyable):
- Internal invite subject: "All-Hands: Company priorities & Q4 OKR preview — Nov X, 10:00 PT"
- Internal invite body: "Please join for a 75-minute townline to align on company priorities, product wins, and what we need from each team next quarter. Bring questions — we’ll have a live Q&A and follow-up doc."

- Post-townline digest subject: "Recap: Townline + Slides + Actions"
- Post-townline digest body: "Thanks all — recording and slides are here [link]. Top three asks: 1) ship caching autopilot pilot (owner), 2) publish token-level cost dashboard (owner), 3) complete upgrade smoke tests (owner). Follow-ups assigned in [triage board link]."

Success metrics for the event (to evaluate in 2 weeks):
- % of employees who say "I understand top-3 priorities" in follow-up pulse (target 80%).
- Number of clarifying threads >5 in Slack down by 60% compared to last all-hands.
- First-week triage completion rate for top-3 asks >= 50%.

Open questions before finalizing (owners assigned):
- Who will represent Legal on the incident statement approval path? (Owner: Samir)
- Which three customers are best fits for caching autopilot beta? (Owner: CS leadership)
- Can Eng-Infra provide a short explainer on how autopilot toggles work without exposing IP? (Owner: Miguel)

Quick next steps (this week):
- Fri 11/15: Leadership dry run (30m) — confirm slides & timing.
- Mon 11/18: Send pre-reads and short survey to collect employee priority questions.
- Wed 11/20: Townline (final) — run-of-show followed.

Appendix (short):
- Contact list: CEO: Aisha Martinez; CTO: Ben Cho; CPO: Lara Singh; People Ops: Nkiru Okonkwo.
- Rehearsal links: [rehearsal-call] (internal calendar).
- Notes to moderator: keep responses <2 minutes, defer complex policy/legal to follow-up doc.

End of doc.
